sentences.text: Coram:- Urmila Joshi-Phalke, J.
DATED :- AUGUST 14, 2024

By preferring this application, the applicant who is bank employee seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with Crime No.130 of 2024 registered on 28/05/2024 at the hands of the Bajaj Nagar Police Station, Nagpur for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 420,
465, 467, 468, 471 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The applicant is apprehending the arrest at the hands of police as the crime is registered on the basis of report lodged by Pukhraj Govardhan Mandan on an allegation that M/s Sirsikar Builders and Developers Pvt Limited had obtained the loan of Rs.5 Crore from the Yavatmal Urban Cooperative Bank Limited, Yavatmal through its Deonagar Branch.

entities.text: Sirsikar Builders and Developers Pvt Limited
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Yavatmal Urban Cooperative Bank Limited, Yavatmal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The informant entered into agreement for purchase of one shop from the said project for total consideration of Rs. 20 Lakh, out of which the complainant paid to the said builder Rs. 5 Lakh and for balance Rs.15 Lakh, he obtained the loan from the Indian Overseas Bank, which was disbursed with two demand drafts of Rs.7.5 Lakh each payable in loan account of said builder.
However, instead of depositing in the loan account, the said amount was deposited in the current account of the said builder.
The informant further alleged that the bank has agreed the said fact of deposit vide its letter dated 11/01/2024.

It is further alleged that the present applicant who is the Branch Manager has also accepted the said amount deposited in the current account instead of loan account and thus he is involved in the crime.

3. Learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that as far as the allegation against the present applicant is concerned, it is only to the extent of that he has accepted the amount in the current account.
Whether there was an intentional act or not is matter of evidence.
At this stage, entire documents are at the bank, the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required.
In view of that he be protected by granting ad-interim protection.

4. He further submitted that the co-accused Raghuveer Padmakar Paithankar who is also a bank employee is already protected by this Court.
5. On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor strongly opposed the said application on the ground that the offence alleged against the present applicant is of a serious nature.
He was under obligation to observe the rules and regulations while accepting the loan amount.
As per his instructions the applicant has contravened the entire guidelines issued by the RBI while disbursing the loan amount.
In view of that, his custodial interrogation is required.

6. After hearing the learned Counsel for the applicant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the non-applicant/State, perused the recitals of the First Information Report from which it reveals that the allegations against the present applicant who was working as a Branch Manager that the bank has accepted the cheque in the current account instead of loan account.
Whether the act was committed in connivance with the other co-accused who is the builder or not is a matter of evidence.
At this stage, entire documents are with the bank.
As far as the recitals of the FIR is concerned which only discloses that the act of the applicant is only to the extent of accepting the cheque in the current account instead of loan account.
In view of that, the immediate custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required and the applicant has made out a case for grant of ad-interim protection.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following order:
(i) Issue notice to the non-applicant, returnable after two weeks.
(ii) Learned APP waives notice for the State and seeks time to file reply.

(iii) In the event of the arrest, the applicant - Aniruddha Madhusudan Tokekar in connection with Crime No.130 of 2024 registered on 28/05/2024 at the hands of the Bajaj Nagar Police Station, Nagpur for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, be released on ad-interim anticipatory bail on executing P.R. bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one solvent surety in the like amount.
(iv) The applicant shall attend the concerned police station once in a week i.e. on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. and 1.00 pm. and shall cooperate with the investigating agency.

(v) The applicant shall not induce, threat or promise any witnesses who are acquainted with the facts of the case.
7.

The present application be tagged along with Criminal Application (ABA) No.578/2024,
568/2024 and 570/2024.
(URMILA JOSHI-PHALKE, J.) *Divya Aniruddha Madhusudan Tokekar vs The State Of Maharashtra Thr.
